sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values
sources.licence: project contribution under the repository's terms

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added with the nightshades work (2026-10-17): every character from the floras in the nightshades notes (plantgen-claude project-files/nightshades/SOURCES.md), drawn by the rules its taxa hold; drawing values only where no character says them.

taxon.note: WCVP v16 accepted name Celastrus scandens, plant_name_id 2707703 (Library 1.0 list, read 2026-10-17).

growth_form.note: Its habit as the floras describe it, drawn by the vine form.

growth.note: Grown to the age it is drawn at: an annual's one season, a perennial's or shrub's few years.

variants.note: One seed in the open, as the built-in species.

generator.params.note: Drawing values no character gives (nightshades, 2026-10-17): two stems from the foot, by eye from a photograph of a vine trailing over rock (iNaturalist 249361238).

traits.life_span.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 2 (1913), Celastrus scandens, p. 493 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): a twining woody vine.

traits.woodiness.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 2 (1913), Celastrus scandens, p. 493 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): a twining woody vine; Small (p. 735): a climbing shrub.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Woody Plant Seed Manual, Agriculture Handbook 727 (2008), Celastrus scandens, p. 363 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): a deciduous climbing or twining shrub.

traits.height_max_m.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 2 (1913), Celastrus scandens, p. 493 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): climbing trees to 25 ft or more, or trailing on the ground; Mathews (1912, p. 254): climbing 6-25 ft; Wikipedia 'Celastrus scandens': 30 ft or more.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 2 (1913), Celastrus scandens, p. 493 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): leaves alternate, somewhat 2-ranked by the twisting of the stem.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 2 (1913), Celastrus scandens, p. 493 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): ovate, oval or obovate; Bailey (vol. 2 p. 701): ovate to ovate-lanceolate.

traits.leaf_apex.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 2 (1913), Celastrus scandens, p. 493 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): acuminate or acute; Small (p. 735): acuminate.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Gray's New Manual, 7th ed. (1908), Celastrus scandens, p. 557 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): finely serrate; Small: serrate; Britton and Brown: crenulate; Bailey: crenate-serrate.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 2 (1913), Celastrus scandens, p. 493 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): 2-4 in long; Small: 6-10 cm; Bailey: 2-4 in.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 2 (1913), Celastrus scandens, p. 493 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): 1-2 in wide.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Small, Flora of the Southeastern United States (1903), Celastrus scandens, p. 735 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): petioles 8-20 mm; Britton and Brown: 6-9 lines (13-19 mm).

traits.leaf_colour.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 2 (1913), Celastrus scandens, p. 493 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): glabrous on both sides; Mathews (1912, p. 254): light green, smooth. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.bark_colour.note: iNaturalist observation 249361238 (CC-licensed photograph, viewed 2026-10-17): the older stems are smooth and grey; Trelease (Winter Botany, 1918, p. 199): twigs brownish, glabrous. No text read gives it.

traits.inflorescence.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 2 (1914-17), Celastrus scandens, p. 701 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): flowers and fruit in terminal, many-flowered panicles or racemes; Britton and Brown: terminal compound racemes.

traits.flowering_position.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 2 (1914-17), Celastrus scandens, p. 701 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): in terminal panicles, carried above the leaves, against C. orbiculatus's axillary cymes.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 2 (1913), Celastrus scandens, p. 493 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): 2-4 in; Bailey: 2-4 in; Small: 4-8 cm.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Small, Flora of the Southeastern United States (1903), Celastrus scandens, p. 735 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): corolla about 8 mm broad; Britton and Brown: about 2 lines (4 mm).

traits.flower_colour.note: Bailey, Standard Cyclopedia of Horticulture vol. 2 (1914-17), Celastrus, p. 700 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): flowers greenish white; Small and Britton and Brown: greenish. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.flowering_months.note: Woody Plant Seed Manual, Agriculture Handbook 727 (2008), Celastrus scandens, p. 363 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): flowers May to June; Gray and Britton and Brown: June.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Britton and Brown, Illustrated Flora, 2nd ed. vol. 2 (1913), Celastrus scandens, p. 493 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): capsule 5-6 lines in diameter (10-13 mm); Small: 1 cm.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Small, Flora of the Southeastern United States (1903), Celastrus scandens, p. 735 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): capsule orange, opening by 3 valves on scarlet arils; Britton and Brown: yellow or orange; Gray: orange. The colour is the valves', our reading of the word.

traits.fruiting_months.note: Woody Plant Seed Manual, Agriculture Handbook 727 (2008), Celastrus scandens, p. 363 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): fruit ripens late August to October, splits soon after and may persist through much of the winter.

host.note: The host it is grown on for rendering, a built-in tree of the same northeastern woods; not a botanical fact.
